subject: Retention handoff, purge timing, and log-exception terms
messages:
From: Emma Taylor <emma.taylor@nexiahealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T08:14:00+01:00
Subject: Initial: retention & purge alignment for NexiaHealth

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for taking this on. NexiaHealth's legal and security teams need confirmation of two items before we can sign the DPA addendum: a) a clear backup purge timeline for customer backups and snapshots (we need to know when backups are irreversibly purged), and b) what log retention exceptions you can provide for audit/e-discovery (we have a pending regulatory review in Q4).

Attached is our retention requirements summary (Nexia_Data_Retention_Requirements.pdf). Specific asks:
- Snapshot retention baseline for EU production workloads (PHI and pseudonymized data considered)
- How long you keep immutable backups and whether you provide a short emergency restore window after purge (we need at least a documented 7-day post-purge restore escrow if possible)
- Subprocessor roster (we need current list and planned changes over the next 90 days)
- Any carveouts for forensic/audit logs (if logs are kept longer, describe isolation/access controls)

Can you confirm your proposed schedule and whether Redwood can commit to an operational exception for audit logs for NexiaHealth? If a contract amendment is needed, please send your redline.

We'd like to close this this week if possible.

Best,
Emma Taylor
Head of Security & Privacy
NexiaHealth

Attachments: Nexia_Data_Retention_Requirements.pdf
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Emma Taylor <emma.taylor@nexiahealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T10:02:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Initial: retention & purge alignment for NexiaHealth

Emma — thanks for the clear ask and the attachment. Summary below of what Redwood can commit to operationally; legal redline attached (Nexia_DPA_v3_redline.pdf) and I've dropped a draft purge cadence spreadsheet into the shared drive (link below).

Proposal (high level):
- Snapshots: standard production snapshot retention is 90 days for EU workloads. Snapshots older than 90 days are marked for purge and queued for irreversible deletion in the next maintenance window.
- Backups (immutable vault): full backup objects are retained for 120 days by default. After day 120 we run a secure purge process that removes keys and rotates storage tombstones; final irreversible deletion occurs during the scheduled purge batch (we can provide a log trace for the purge event).
- Emergency restore escrow: Redwood can offer a 14-day emergency restore hold after purge attribution for NexiaHealth as a paid addendum — operationally we mark eligible backups with an escrow tag and retain a recoverability manifest for 14 days after the purge event to support restores.
- Audit/forensic logs: standard access/audit logs are retained for 180 days. For regulatory audits we can provide a scoped log-exception for select audit streams up to 365 days; those streams are separated into an encrypted partition with restricted key access and documented access procedures.
- Subprocessors: attached is current subprocessor roster (see DPA redline). Planned subprocessor changes in the next 90 days are limited to one new caching vendor for EU-edge (we will notify Nexia 30 days in advance and provide SOC/attestations).

Operational caveats:
- The 14-day escrow is implementable but requires a signed amendment (we've attached the redline) and will be tied to a modest monthly fee to cover additional retention costs.
- Any carveout extending log retention beyond 365 days requires legal sign-off and an SLA exception (we can't extend for all customers as it increases security/replication cost).

Next steps:
1) Kimberly, Laura: can you confirm wording and whether finance needs to estimate the recurring escrow fee?
2) Emma & Jeff: if these operational points are acceptable, we'll send the DPA redline + amendment via DocuSign for signature.

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cNexiaRetention

--
Priyom Das
Senior Product Manager, Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Nexia_DPA_v3_redline.pdf
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T11:20:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Initial: retention & purge alignment for NexiaHealth

Team — quick compliance note and a suggested operational split to reduce cost impact:

- For non-PHI datasets we can offer a reduced snapshot retention of 45 days (instead of 90) if Nexia is comfortable with a classification tag to mark PHI-sensitivity. That will reduce the number of objects queued for purge and the escrow surface.
- I've attached a proposed schedule (backup_timeline.xlsx) that shows two lanes: PHI lane (90/120/14-escrow) and Non-PHI lane (45/90/7-escrow) with cost deltas.
- On log exceptions: we will only allow the 365-day exception for specific audit streams with documented retention reasons (regulatory + legal hold). We also need a contract clause that requires Nexia to request a log hold with a ticket and specify scope + justification; we'll retain the right to deny if it exceeds reasonable scope.

Marcus — can you confirm that the escrow manifest and restore playbook are ready from an ops standpoint? Laura — please flag if procurement needs a PO or SOW before we enable the escrow.

Thanks,
Kimberly
Director, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

Attachments: backup_timeline.xlsx
From: Jeff Chen <jeff.chen@nexiahealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Taylor <emma.taylor@nexiahealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T15:03:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Initial: retention & purge alignment for NexiaHealth

Priyom / Kimberly — thanks for the thorough reply. Nexia is generally comfortable with the two-lane approach (PHI vs Non-PHI). Two quick items before we move to signature:

1) Please send the DocuSign link for the DPA amendment + escrow fee schedule so procurement can route it.
2) For the 365-day log exception, we need explicit language that Redwood will provide an access audit for any extended logs and that logs will remain encrypted with separate keys. Can you add a clause and the operational playbook excerpt to the redline?

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if that speeds things up — our availability tomorrow 0900-1200 CEST.

Thanks,
Jeff Chen
Procurement Lead
NexiaHealth
